items.stem: Distinguish between 'self-efficacy' and 'self-regulation'.
items.answer: Self-efficacy: a person's belief in his or her ability to control life outcomes, a concept given by Albert Bandura. Self-regulation: the ability to organise and monitor one's own behaviour, including delaying gratification.

items.stem: Read the case and answer. Nikhil believes that if he practises daily he can surely learn to swim, even though he cannot swim yet. Name the aspect of self shown here and explain it briefly.
items.answer: Self-efficacy: self-efficacy is the belief that one can achieve a goal through one's own actions.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: 1 mark for naming it (self-efficacy); 1 mark for the explanation (self-efficacy is the belief that one can achieve a goal through one's own actions).

items.stem: The concept of the collective unconscious was given by:
items.answer: Carl Jung
items.markingKey: (d) Carl Jung.
options: Alfred Adler
Karen Horney
Sigmund Freud
Carl Jung

items.stem: Read the case and answer. Suresh is always in a hurry, impatient in queues, competitive and easily irritated by delays. Identify the personality type illustrated.
items.answer: Type-A personality.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Type-A personality.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about psychodynamic, behavioural, cultural and humanistic approaches is NOT correct?
items.answer: According to Freud, the superego works on the pleasure principle.
items.markingKey: (d) It is incorrect. The id works on the pleasure principle; the superego is the moral branch.
options: Behaviourists see personality as a set of learned responses to stimuli.
Humanistic theorists emphasise growth, free will and self-actualisation.
The cultural approach explains personality as an adaptation to the ecology and culture of a group.
According to Freud, the superego works on the pleasure principle.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Self-regulation is important for achieving long-term goals.
Reason (R): It allows people to resist temptations and delay immediate gratification.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Both are true and R explains A: it allows people to resist temptations and delay immediate gratification.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: In the study of assessment of personality, the term 'social desirability' refers to:
items.answer: The tendency of respondents to give answers that are socially acceptable rather than true
items.markingKey: (c) 'social desirability' means the tendency of respondents to give answers that are socially acceptable rather than true.
options: Raymond Cattell's term for the stable, basic traits that form the core of personality, measured by the 16 PF
Assessment of personality through interviews, observation, ratings, nomination and situational tests
The tendency of respondents to give answers that are socially acceptable rather than true
A person's belief in his or her ability to control life outcomes, a concept given by Albert Bandura

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about type and trait approaches to personality is NOT correct?
items.answer: Cattell proposed the Big Five factors.
items.markingKey: (b) It is incorrect. Costa and McCrae proposed the Big Five; Cattell identified 16 source traits.
options: Traits are relatively stable over time and consistent across situations.
Cattell proposed the Big Five factors.
Hippocrates classified people into four types based on body fluids.
The triguna approach classifies personality by the qualities of sattva, rajas and tamas.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on the concept of self and answer the questions that follow.
"The self develops through interaction with other people. The Indian view of self is more collectivistic, while the Western view is more individualistic. Self-regulation includes the ability to resist situational pressures and delay gratification."
(i) The ability to delay or defer the gratification of needs is part of: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'self' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: People with high self-efficacy are more likely to succeed. (2)
items.answer: (i) self-regulation (ii) The totality of a person's conscious experiences, ideas, thoughts and feelings with regard to himself or herself. (iii) They believe in their ability to control outcomes and so persist in the face of difficulty.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) self-regulation (ii) The totality of a person's conscious experiences, ideas, thoughts and feelings with regard to himself or herself. (iii) They believe in their ability to control outcomes and so persist in the face of difficulty.

items.stem: Read the case and answer. Ankit failed to get into the cricket team and told everyone that he never really wanted to play. Identify the defence mechanism illustrated.
items.answer: Rationalisation.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: rationalisation.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about assessment of personality is NOT correct?
items.answer: Projective tests use clear, unambiguous stimuli.
items.markingKey: (a) It is incorrect. They use ambiguous stimuli.
options: Projective tests use clear, unambiguous stimuli.
Scoring of projective techniques requires trained and experienced psychologists.
Self-report measures can be affected by social desirability and acquiescence.
Projective tests use relatively ambiguous stimuli.

items.stem: "The Big Five model is widely accepted." Examine this statement with reference to type and trait approaches to personality.
items.answer: The statement is valid. Its five factors have been found in many cultures and are useful for understanding personality.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: 1 for accepting or qualifying the statement, 1 for the reason (its five factors have been found in many cultures and are useful for understanding personality.), 1 for supporting evidence from the chapter.

items.stem:
Statement: Freud believed that unconscious conflicts shape behaviour.
Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: Many desires unacceptable to society are pushed into the unconscious, from where they influence thoughts and actions.
items.markingKey: (a) Many desires unacceptable to society are pushed into the unconscious, from where they influence thoughts and actions.
options: Many desires unacceptable to society are pushed into the unconscious, from where they influence thoughts and actions.
These reduce anxiety caused by conflicts between the id, ego and superego, though they distort reality.
People develop a healthy self-concept when they are accepted without conditions.
They believe in their ability to control outcomes and so persist in the face of difficulty.

items.stem: In the study of psychodynamic, behavioural, cultural and humanistic approaches, the term 'ego' refers to:
items.answer: In Freud's theory, the part of personality that works on the reality principle and mediates between the id and the superego
items.markingKey: (c) 'ego' means in Freud's theory, the part of personality that works on the reality principle and mediates between the id and the superego.
options: A way of reducing anxiety by distorting reality, such as repression, projection or denial
The approach that groups people into distinct categories on the basis of broad patterns of behaviour
In Freud's theory, the part of personality that works on the reality principle and mediates between the id and the superego
In Maslow's theory, the state in which people have reached their full potential

items.stem: Give a reason for the following: Scoring of projective tests needs trained psychologists.
items.answer: Responses are open-ended and must be interpreted, which requires skill and experience.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: Responses are open-ended and must be interpreted, which requires skill and experience. (1 mark for the reason, 1 for linking it to the statement).

items.stem:

items.answer: Indian culture is collectivistic, so the self includes family and community, while Western culture emphasises individual autonomy.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on type and trait approaches to personality and answer the questions that follow.
"The Big Five model is useful for understanding personality across cultures. Type-C personality is said to be prone to cancer, and Type-D to depression. The triguna approach classifies personality by the qualities of sattva, rajas and tamas."
(i) Hans Eysenck described personality in terms of neuroticism versus emotional stability and: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'type approach' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Type approaches have been criticised. (2)
items.answer: (i) extraversion versus introversion (ii) The approach that groups people into distinct categories on the basis of broad patterns of behaviour. (iii) Human behaviour is too complex to fit neatly into a small number of types.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) extraversion versus introversion (ii) The approach that groups people into distinct categories on the basis of broad patterns of behaviour. (iii) Human behaviour is too complex to fit neatly into a small number of types.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about the concept of self is correct?
items.answer: The self develops through interaction with other people.
items.markingKey: (d) The others are wrong: The Western view is individualistic with clear boundaries; the Indian view is more flexible. That is personal identity; social identity links a person to groups. That is self-esteem; self-efficacy is the belief in one's ability to achieve outcomes.
options: Social identity refers to attributes that make a person different from others.
Self-efficacy refers to the value judgement about oneself.
The Western view of self has flexible boundaries that include the family.
The self develops through interaction with other people.
